    AI Overview
    As of April 2026, discussions regarding the 25th Amendment and Donald Trump have resurfaced, with some calling for
    Section 4 to be invoked following aggressive rhetoric on social media, including threats regarding Iran. This constitutional provision allows the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet to remove a president deemed unable to discharge their duties. 
    Key Aspects of the 25th Amendment Discussion (2026): 
    • Triggering Events: Reports indicate calls for removal followed Trump's "unhinged" Easter social media posts containing threats against the Strait of Hormuz.
    • The Process: Under Section 4, if the President contests their removal, the Vice President keeps power only if two-thirds of both the House and Senate agree.
    • Context: The 25th Amendment, which has never been used, was previously discussed regarding Trump in 2021 following the Capitol riot.
    • Political Dynamics: Observers note that such a move is a high bar, requiring near-unanimity in the cabinet and facing intense political opposition, often described as an "unworkable", high-stakes move. 
    This renewed debate centers on questions about President Trump's fitness for office and the potential for a Cabinet-led effort to transfer power.

    People also ask
    Who can invoke the 25th Amendment to remove a president?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The 25th Amendment (Section 4) can be invoked against a U.S. President by the
    Vice President acting together with a majority of the principal officers of the executive departments (the Cabinet). They must submit a written declaration to Congress stating the President is unable to discharge their powers and duties. 
    • Who Initiates: The Vice President leads this process.
    • Who Must Agree: A majority of the Cabinet secretaries (or another body designated by Congress).
    • Actionable Step: They submit a written declaration to the President Pro Tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House.
    • Result:
      The Vice President immediately becomes the Acting President.
    • If the President Contests: If the President declares they are fit, the Vice President and Cabinet have four days to contest this, and Congress must assemble within 48 hours to decide the issue. A two-thirds vote in both houses of Congress is required to keep the Vice President in power. 
    This section has never been invoked in U.S. history.
